newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA'S 1997/98 MILK OUTPUT QUOTA CUT 2.9 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CANADA'S 1997/98 MILK OUTPUT QUOTA CUT 2.9 PCT.

text.p: The Canadian Milk Supply Management Committee cut the national Market Share Quota (MSQ) by 2.9 percent in marketing year 1997/98 (Aug/July), a joint statement by the Alberta Dairy Control Board and Alberta Milk Producers said.
The MSQ was cut to 42.6 million hectolitres in 1997/98 from 43.9 million hectolitres in 1996/97, the statement said.
The Market Share Quota dictates how much total milk farmers can market in the marketing year.

"Canadian consumers are choosing different types of dairy products, eating less ice cream and more cheese, but also purchasing lower fat milk and dairy products," AMP chairman Robert Krueger said in the statement.
"This fact means that less milk fat is needed to manufacture the types of dairy products Canadian consumers want," Krueger added.
About 2,200 tonnes of butter was imported into Canada in compliance with international trade obligations Canada adopted, the statement said.
